items.explanation: 71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation documented 2025-08-22 (ICD-9 42731) and carried in every cardiology clinic note through 2026-07-28. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1); no CHF, diabetes or prior stroke/TIA. Current medication list is tamsulosin only - no oral anticoagulant has ever been ordered. Guideline-recommended anticoagulation (CHA2DS2-VASc >=2 in a man) is absent; needs prescriber review. Remote hemorrhage complicating a procedure (2025-08-22) should be weighed but is not an active contraindication.

35-year-old woman on citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, continuously since 2023-10-02 (current order 2026-05-29 to 2026-12-25); 40 mg is also above the recommended maximum for QT safety. Her most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10, five weeks after citalopram was started) shows sinus rhythm 70 bpm, QT 490 ms, Bazett QTc 529 ms - above the 500 ms threshold of the 2025-01-15 QT monitoring memo, and up from QTc 465 ms in 2020. Hypothyroidism and prior acute kidney failure add risk. Prescriber review required; no ECG has been repeated in nearly three years. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21), magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01).

95-year-old woman on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) since 2022, current order 2026-08-22 to 2027-01-05, with warfarin and metoprolol. Her most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus rhythm at 57 bpm with a markedly prolonged QT of 546 ms, Bazett QTc 534 ms - above the 500 ms threshold of the 2025-01-15 QT monitoring memo (up from QTc 443 ms during AF three weeks earlier). Prescriber review required, and no ECG has been repeated in over four years while amiodarone continues. Most recent electrolytes (2026-02-14): potassium 4.1 mEq/L, magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (low-normal).

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was newly started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-03-02. Because the start is on/after 2026-03-01, the revised 2026-03-01 memo applies and an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 2026-03-07, five days after the start - requirement met. That ECG shows sinus rhythm 81 bpm with QTc 378 ms (no prolongation).

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was newly started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2025-11-10. The start falls between 2025-09-01 and 2026-03-01, so the 2025-09-01 memo applies and an ECG is required within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start - requirement met. Note that ECG shows QTc 520 ms, which itself triggers a separate QT safety review.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was newly started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-02-12. The start is before 2026-03-01, so the earlier 30-day window of the 2025-09-01 memo applies (expressly preserved by the 2026-03-01 revision), giving a due date of 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start - requirement met (sinus rhythm 68 bpm, QTc 444 ms).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was newly started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-04-10. Start on/after 2026-03-01, so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, due 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was recorded 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start - outside the required 14-day window, so the requirement was not met within time and is overdue as of the evaluation date. The late ECG showed sinus rhythm 69 bpm, QTc 378 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was newly started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (it was absent from the 2026-06-24 medication list). Start on/after 2026-03-01, so an ECG is required within 14 days, due 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25 (before the start), so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was newly started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-10. Start on/after 2026-03-01, so an ECG is required within 14 days, due 2026-08-24. The nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and no ECG exists in the chart for this patient. Whether the requirement was satisfied cannot be determined until the outside tracing is obtained.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was newly started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-09-15. Start on/after 2026-03-01, so an ECG is required within 14 days, due 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09, but the due date is after the 2026-09-24 evaluation time, so the requirement is not yet due. It should be tracked (chronic kidney disease and psychotic disorder on haloperidol).

Cardiology clinic note of 2026-09-01 by Dr. Paul Kessler documents INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increases warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 2026-03-01 memo an INR is required within 7 days of a dose change made by a clinic clinician, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, four days after the change - requirement met.

80-year-old woman whose cardiology clinic notes of 2025-09-12, 2025-12-31, 2026-03-12 and 2026-05-28 all document persistent atrial fibrillation in the active problem list. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (CHF - hypertensive heart disease with heart failure / acute on chronic systolic and diastolic heart failure 1; hypertension 1; age >=75 2; type 2 diabetes 1; prior cerebral infarction / TIA with residual dysarthria and hemiplegia 2; vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis and old myocardial infarction 1; female 1). Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin only, with no anticoagulant order at any time. Very high stroke risk AF with no anticoagulation - needs prescriber review.

Anticoagulation clinic note of 2026-09-10 by L. Nguyen, PharmD (a clinic pharmacist acting under the anticoagulation standing order) documents home INR 3.4 and decreases warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily. Under the 2026-03-01 memo an INR is required within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. The last INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22; no INR has been resulted since the dose change, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24 in a 95-year-old on warfarin plus amiodarone.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded 2025-03-14 (ICD-10 I48.0). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior cerebral infarction due to embolism with residual left hemiparesis 2, female 1). Current medications through the 2026-07-10 clinic visit are famotidine, metoprolol tartrate and carvedilol; no anticoagulant has ever been ordered. Guideline-recommended anticoagulation is absent in a patient with prior cardioembolic stroke - needs prescriber review (thrombocytopenia noted 2025-03-14 should be considered).

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation carried in the problem list of every cardiology clinic note from 2025-07-19 through 2026-06-12 (also coded as other specified cardiac dysrhythmias 2025-06-17 during the admission in which AF was managed). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive/acute systolic heart failure with cardiomyopathy documented 2025-02-26 = 1; essential hypertension = 1); age <65, no diabetes, stroke or vascular disease. A CHA2DS2-VASc of 2 in a man carries a guideline recommendation for oral anticoagulation, but current medications are only famotidine and pantoprazole - the long-term anticoagulant use coded in June 2025 was not continued. Needs prescriber review.

74-year-old man with atrial flutter on apixaban 5 mg twice daily plus aspirin and clopidogrel. Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document admission 8/2-8/5/2026 with upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused, and apixaban HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite this, apixaban 5 mg BID was re-ordered on 2026-08-20 (valid to 2026-12-28) and the 2026-08-20 clinic note states continue current regimen, with triple therapy (apixaban + aspirin + clopidogrel) still in place. A current anticoagulant is being continued against a documented recent major GI bleed and an explicit hold pending review.

Two overlapping direct oral anticoagulant orders are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 cardiology note states the intention was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban order was renewed rather than stopped and both appear on the medication list. Duplicate anticoagulation in a patient with AF/flutter and CLL creates a major bleeding hazard and must be reconciled.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72. Both ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response at 139 and 144 bpm with no discernible P waves - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded that day. The note rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day ECGs.

Patient takes escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current order 2026-04-23 to 2027-01-02, continuously since 2024-05-14). His most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) is sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 482 ms and Bazett QTc 516 ms - at or above the 500 ms threshold in the 2025-01-15 QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. The 2024-05-14 note characterised that ECG as QT acceptable, which understates the measured interval. Most recent electrolytes (2025-08-23) are normal: potassium 4.1 mEq/L, magnesium 2.1 mg/dL. No ECG has been obtained since escitalopram continued.

79-year-old man on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; started at the 2025-11-10 cardiology clinic visit, current order 2026-07-29 to 2027-01-05) together with warfarin. His most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24, obtained for the post-start monitoring requirement) shows sinus rhythm 62 bpm, QRS 102 ms, QT 512 ms, Bazett QTc 520 ms - above the 500 ms threshold of the 2025-01-15 QT monitoring memo, and markedly increased from QTc 413 ms on the pre-amiodarone ECG of 2025-06-07. Prescriber review required. Most recent electrolytes (2026-04-20) normal: potassium 4.4 mEq/L, magnesium 2.2 mg/dL.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with gentle rate variation. Normal PR 182 ms, narrow QRS 86 ms, QT 326 ms giving Bazett QTc 378 ms. Frontal QRS axis about +50 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. This is the patient first and only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible. Recorded at the 2026-03-07 cardiology visit 5 days after citalopram was started; the rhythm agrees with the note (sinus) and the QTc is not prolonged.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 104 bpm, regular (RR 568-586 ms), upright P in lead II with PR 126 ms. QRS 104 ms, QT 336 ms, Bazett QTc 442 ms. Axis about +40 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2025-06-20 showed sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm (RR 380-424 ms, P waves visible) with QRS 100 ms and a QTc of roughly 470 ms on a noisy baseline; rate has slowed but rhythm, conduction and QTc show no qualifying change.

Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm, regular (RR 538-614 ms) with low-amplitude upright P waves in lead II, PR 112 ms. QRS 96 ms, QT 334 ms, Bazett QTc 451 ms. Frontal axis about +39 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Single ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 144 bpm: RR intervals range 344-648 ms (RMSSD 97 ms, 60 percent of successive intervals differing by more than 50 ms) and there is no organised atrial activity, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 102 ms, QT 294 ms, Bazett QTc 455 ms. Frontal axis about 0 to -5 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG earlier the same evening (107914094, 17:13) already showed atrial fibrillation at 139 bpm with QRS 104 ms and QTc 451 ms - no change. Note the 2026-06-10 clinic note describes this as normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, which the tracings contradict.

Sinus rhythm 69 bpm, very regular (RR 864-884 ms), P waves present with PR 142 ms. QRS 88 ms, QT 406 ms, Bazett QTc 435 ms. Net frontal forces give an axis of about -29 degrees, at the border of normal and left axis deviation but within the normal range; lead I and aVL are strongly positive with a deep S in III (borderline left axis). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2025-04-27 (sinus 60 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 407 ms) showed an inverted complex in I with positive aVR, consistent with limb-lead reversal on that recording; rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular (RR 596-628 ms), upright P waves in lead II with a short PR of 106 ms. QRS 80 ms, QT 312 ms, Bazett QTc 398 ms. Frontal axis about +7 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular (RR 820-840 ms), clear upright P waves with PR 136 ms. QRS 88 ms, QT 379 ms, Bazett QTc 415 ms. Frontal axis about +22 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison. This tracing predates the escitalopram started on 2026-08-01, for which a post-start ECG is still outstanding.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response, mean 53 bpm: RR intervals 694-1164 ms, irregularly irregular (RMSSD 288 ms, 62 percent of successive differences above 50 ms), with no identifiable P wave (candidate atrial deflection 0.07 mV versus 0.05 mV baseline noise), so no PR interval. QRS 98 ms, QT 427 ms, Bazett QTc 401 ms. Axis about +17 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2024-11-12 showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with clear P waves and PR 172 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new since that tracing; QTc essentially unchanged (399 to 401 ms).

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with slight sinus irregularity (RR 976-1082 ms); upright P waves in II with a short PR of 104 ms. QRS 92 ms, QT 416 ms, Bazett QTc 410 ms. Deep S waves in V2-V3 without conduction delay. Frontal axis about +62 degrees (normal). Compared with the prior ECG of 2025-03-08 (sinus 62 bpm, PR 106 ms, QRS 94 ms, QTc 435 ms) there is no significant change.

Normal sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, highly regular (RR 716-726 ms), upright P waves with PR 140 ms. Narrow QRS 78 ms, QT 344 ms, Bazett QTc 405 ms. Frontal axis about +56 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, regular (RR 774-804 ms), prominent upright P waves in lead II with PR 148 ms. Narrow QRS 76 ms, QT 400 ms, Bazett QTc 452 ms (mildly prolonged). Frontal axis about +67 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 2020-02-02 was a very low-voltage tracing (limb-lead amplitudes under 0.2 mV) with a similarly narrow QRS complex and a flat late T wave; measured QTc was comparable (about 515 ms on that noisy tracing) and no rhythm or conduction change can be established between the two.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, metronomically regular (RR 494-502 ms) with an upright P before every QRS. PR 158 ms, QRS 102 ms, QT 288 ms, Bazett QTc 408 ms. Axis about +50 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Compared with the prior tracing of 2016-09-16 (sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, PR 178 ms, QRS 98 ms, QTc 400 ms) the rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged; only the rate is a little faster.

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm, regular (RR 1074-1118 ms). The P wave in lead II begins about 205 ms before QRS onset, i.e. first-degree AV block (PR just above 200 ms). QRS 88 ms with tall R waves and deep S in V2-V3 (large precordial voltages), QT 395 ms, Bazett QTc 376 ms. Frontal axis about 0 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2024-11-30 was sinus bradycardia at 51 bpm with PR 184 ms, QRS 88 ms and QTc 360 ms - the PR has lengthened slightly across the 200 ms threshold but rhythm, QRS and QTc are otherwise unchanged.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 153 bpm: RR intervals 288-580 ms, chaotically irregular (RMSSD 104 ms, 52 percent of successive differences above 50 ms) with no organised atrial activity, so no measurable PR. Low-amplitude QRS of 102 ms, QT 274 ms, Bazett QTc 437 ms. Frontal axis about -25 degrees (normal, borderline leftward). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of the previous evening (107374881, 2025-09-12) showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with PR 144 ms after one early beat, so the atrial fibrillation is new; QTc unchanged (411 to 437 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm (RR 788-922 ms), upright P waves in lead II with PR 168 ms. QRS 98 ms, QT 356 ms, Bazett QTc 394 ms. Frontal axis about +14 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2025-11-21 (sinus 67 bpm, PR 150 ms, QRS 96 ms, QT 502 ms, QTc 532 ms with a markedly delayed broad T wave) the QTc has fallen by about 138 ms, well beyond the 60 ms threshold, with normalisation of repolarisation. Rhythm, axis and conduction are unchanged. This tracing matches the 2025-11-23 note documenting sinus rhythm.

Normal sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, regular (RR 802-822 ms), upright P waves with PR 178 ms. QRS 92 ms with low overall voltage and a terminal S wave in I/aVL with terminal R in III, but duration is normal so no bundle branch block. QT 380 ms, Bazett QTc 423 ms. Frontal axis about +60 degrees (normal). Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, extremely regular (RR 536-542 ms) with large upright P waves in lead II and PR 160 ms. QRS 100 ms with a very deep QS complex in V1-V2 (anteroseptal forces) but normal duration - no bundle branch block. QT 294 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. Frontal axis about +39 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2022-07-04 (sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, PR 166 ms, QRS 102 ms, QTc 400 ms) is essentially identical; no change.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm. The underlying rhythm is regular at about 980 ms with a single early beat followed by a compensatory pause (RR sequence 982, 984, 544, 1368, 978 ms), so the high overall RR variability is due to one ectopic beat rather than atrial fibrillation; a discrete P wave precedes each sinus QRS with PR about 195 ms (within normal limits). QRS 106 ms, QT 373 ms, Bazett QTc 377 ms. Net frontal forces point up and left - lead I and aVL strongly positive, II and aVF negative - axis about -35 degrees (left axis deviation). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; the paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded the same day is not captured on this tracing.

Regular rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 838-884 ms) with a consistent atrial deflection before each QRS, PR 136 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 98 ms, QT 352 ms, Bazett QTc 378 ms. The frontal plane complexes are inverted in I, II and aVL with a positive aVR, giving a computed axis of about -171 degrees, i.e. in the extreme (northwest) quadrant; this pattern is typical of right/left arm lead reversal and the limb leads should be re-recorded before the axis is accepted as real. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison. It was recorded 2026-04-29, outside the 14-day window after escitalopram was started on 2026-04-10.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm (RR 800-892 ms), upright P waves with PR 148 ms. QRS 102 ms, axis about +45 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is clearly prolonged with a broad late T wave: QT 490 ms, Bazett QTc 529 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 2020-06-17 (sinus tachycardia 132 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 102 ms, QT 313 ms, QTc 465 ms) the QTc has increased by about 64 ms, meeting the 60 ms threshold. The patient is on citalopram 40 mg daily, so this requires QT safety review.

Normal sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR 860-900 ms), upright P waves in lead II with PR 138 ms. QRS 88 ms, QT 417 ms, Bazett QTc 444 ms (upper normal). Frontal axis about +60 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison. Recorded 2026-03-08 to satisfy the post-start ECG requirement for escitalopram begun 2026-02-12; QTc is below the 500 ms review threshold.

Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm with gradual slowing through the recording (RR 1112-1170 ms); upright P waves in lead II with PR 170 ms. QRS 96 ms, QT 378 ms, Bazett QTc 355 ms. Frontal axis about -5 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2018-12-13 was sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with PR 198 ms, QRS 104 ms and QTc 387 ms; the PR has shortened slightly and no qualifying change is present.

Sinus rhythm 68 bpm, PR 124 ms, QRS 94 ms, axis about +49 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. The repolarisation is markedly abnormal: a long flat ST segment with a late low-amplitude T wave peaking near 400 ms, QT 482 ms and Bazett QTc 516 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 2022-11-23 (sinus 74 bpm, QT 323 ms, QTc 361 ms) the QTc has increased by about 155 ms, far beyond the 60 ms threshold. Rhythm, axis and conduction are otherwise unchanged. The patient takes escitalopram, so this warrants QT safety review; the 2024-05-14 note describing the QT as acceptable is inconsistent with the measurement.

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm (RR 402-454 ms, RMSSD only 12 ms). There is no upright sinus P wave; instead a repetitive atrial deflection is seen at twice the ventricular rate (atrial cycle about 212 ms, roughly 280 per minute), negative in II, III and aVF and positive in V1 - the morphology of typical counter-clockwise atrial flutter with 2:1 AV conduction. No PR interval is measurable. QRS 86 ms, QT 277 ms, Bazett QTc 424 ms. Frontal axis about +3 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block, and no pacing spikes despite the pacemaker in situ. The prior ECG of 2022-07-11 showed atrial fibrillation (RR 380-822 ms, RMSSD 189 ms, no organised atrial activity), so the tracing now shows new organised atrial flutter with resolution of fibrillation; QTc unchanged.

Normal sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, regular (RR 710-738 ms), upright P waves in lead II beginning about 168 ms before the QRS. QRS 106 ms - slightly wide but without a bundle branch block pattern (no terminal R in V1, no broad monophasic R in V6). QT 371 ms, Bazett QTc 434 ms. Frontal axis about +33 degrees (normal). Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, regular (RR 650-666 ms), with a broad but clearly upright P wave in lead II starting about 185 ms before QRS onset - PR at the upper limit of normal but below 200 ms, so no first-degree AV block. QRS 84 ms, QT 337 ms, Bazett QTc 415 ms. Frontal axis about -10 to -19 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2021-05-16 (sinus 87 bpm, PR 138 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 395 ms) the PR is longer and the axis slightly more leftward, but there is no qualifying rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with occasional irregularity (RR 954-1196 ms). The P wave starts about 210 ms before the QRS - first-degree AV block. QRS is broad at 136 ms with a deep QS/rS complex in V1-V4 (V3 to -2.7 mV), a broad monophasic R in lead I, aVL and V6 and no septal q waves: left bundle branch block. QT 444 ms, Bazett QTc 448 ms. Net frontal axis about -25 degrees (within the normal range, borderline leftward). Compared with the prior ECG of 2024-06-03 (sinus 68 bpm, PR about 205 ms, QRS 136 ms with the same left bundle branch block morphology, QTc 456 ms) there is no change - the block and AV delay were already present.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm, regular (RR 580-596 ms), upright P waves in lead II with PR 130 ms. QRS 96 ms, QT 330 ms, Bazett QTc 430 ms. Frontal axis about +48 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of the previous afternoon (101016166: sinus 102 bpm, PR 124 ms, QRS 94 ms, QTc 424 ms) the tracings are essentially identical - no change.

Normal sinus rhythm at 66 bpm, regular (RR 904-934 ms), upright P wave in lead II with PR 152 ms. QRS 96 ms with very low precordial voltage, QT 370 ms, Bazett QTc 387 ms. Frontal axis about -24 degrees (normal, borderline leftward; qR in I/aVL with rS in III). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus bradycardia at 57 bpm (RR 970-1100 ms) with a discrete upright P wave in lead II before every QRS, PR about 190 ms (upper normal, no AV block). QRS 94 ms. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a very broad late T wave: QT 546 ms, Bazett QTc 534 ms. Frontal axis about +38 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2022-04-06 showed atrial fibrillation at 131 bpm (RR 324-616 ms, RMSSD 136 ms, no organised P waves) with QT 300 ms and QTc 443 ms, so sinus rhythm has been restored (resolved atrial fibrillation) but the QTc has increased by about 91 ms, beyond the 60 ms threshold - relevant to ongoing amiodarone therapy.

Sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm, extremely regular (RR 554-562 ms), prominent upright P waves in lead II with PR 178 ms. Narrow QRS 78 ms, QT 332 ms, Bazett QTc 444 ms. Frontal axis about +55 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2019-07-27 (sinus 75 bpm, PR 150 ms, QRS 76 ms, QT 378 ms, QTc 422 ms) the rate is faster but rhythm, conduction and QTc show no qualifying change.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, regular (RR 492-500 ms), with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS. PR 124 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 306 ms, Bazett QTc 434 ms. Frontal axis about +70 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at the upper limit of normal, 101 bpm, regular with upright P waves and PR 138 ms. QRS 96 ms, QT 324 ms, Bazett QTc 421 ms. Axis about +60 degrees (normal). Prominent precordial voltages with deep S waves in V1-V3 but no bundle branch block. The prior tracing was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same morning (102910502: sinus 100 bpm, PR 136 ms, QRS 96 ms, QTc 417 ms) and is essentially identical - no interval change.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, very regular (RR 1144-1176 ms), with a small upright P wave in lead II and PR 162 ms. QRS 96 ms with very large precordial voltages (V4-V6 up to 4 mV) suggesting left ventricular hypertrophy. QT 434 ms, Bazett QTc 403 ms. Axis about +40 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block; despite the coded Mobitz II AV block there is no dropped beat on this tracing. Compared with the prior ECG of 2023-05-22 (sinus 57 bpm with one early beat and a pause, PR 146 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 394 ms) there is no significant change.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, extremely regular (RR 492-496 ms), P waves upright in II with PR 158 ms. Low-voltage QRS of 98 ms with an RS pattern in lead I and a small terminal r in V1 (incomplete right bundle branch block pattern only); QT 305 ms, Bazett QTc 434 ms. Net frontal QRS forces are directed rightward, axis about +130 degrees (right axis deviation). Compared with the earlier tracing the same day (106516875, 01:33: sinus 100 bpm with QRS 158 ms, broad terminal R in V1-V3 and terminal S in I/V6 - complete right bundle branch block, QTc 473 ms) the bundle branch block has resolved and the QRS has narrowed to 98 ms; QTc is not significantly different.

Sinus rhythm 62 bpm, regular, PR 164 ms, QRS 102 ms, axis about +65 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is prolonged with a late broad T wave: QT 512 ms, Bazett QTc 520 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 2025-06-07 (sinus bradycardia 47 bpm with marked sinus irregularity, PR 178 ms, QRS 104 ms, QT 466 ms, QTc 413 ms) the QTc has risen by about 107 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold; rhythm, axis and conduction are unchanged. The interval change follows the start of amiodarone on 2025-11-10 and requires QT safety review.

Atrial fibrillation: the ventricular response is grossly irregular (RR 388-1070 ms, RMSSD 249 ms, 73 percent of successive intervals differing by more than 50 ms) and no organised P wave can be identified (the pre-QRS deflection is no larger than the baseline noise), so no PR interval is measurable. Mean ventricular rate 99 bpm. QRS 88 ms, QT 318 ms, Bazett QTc 408 ms using the median RR. Frontal axis about -55 degrees (left axis deviation). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; it corresponds to the atrial fibrillation coded on 2024-09-16.

The prior ECG of 2022-07-11 showed atrial fibrillation (RR 380-822 ms, RMSSD 189 ms, no organised atrial activity), so the tracing now shows new organised atrial flutter with resolution of fibrillation; QTc unchanged.

No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; the paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded the same day is not captured on this tracing.

Regular rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 838-884 ms) with a consistent atrial deflection before each QRS, PR 136 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 98 ms, QT 352 ms, Bazett QTc 378 ms. The frontal plane complexes are inverted in I, II and aVL with a positive aVR, giving a computed axis of about -171 degrees, i.e. in the extreme (northwest) quadrant; this pattern is typical of right/left arm lead reversal and the limb leads should be re-recorded before the axis is accepted as real. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison. It was recorded 2026-04-29, outside the 14-day window after escitalopram was started on 2026-04-10.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm (RR 800-892 ms), upright P waves with PR 148 ms. QRS 102 ms, axis about +45 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm (RR 402-454 ms, RMSSD only 12 ms). The prior ECG of 2022-07-11 showed atrial fibrillation (RR 380-822 ms, RMSSD 189 ms, no organised atrial activity), so the tracing now shows new organised atrial flutter with resolution of fibrillation; QTc unchanged.

Compared with the prior ECG of 2025-03-08 (sinus 62 bpm, PR 106 ms, QRS 94 ms, QTc 435 ms) there is no significant change.

Normal sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, highly regular (RR 716-726 ms), upright P waves with PR 140 ms. Narrow QRS 78 ms, QT 344 ms, Bazett QTc 405 ms. Frontal axis about +56 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, regular (RR 774-804 ms), prominent upright P waves in lead II with PR 148 ms. Narrow QRS 76 ms, QT 400 ms, Bazett QTc 452 ms (mildly prolonged). Frontal axis about +67 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 2020-02-02 was a very low-voltage tracing (limb-lead amplitudes under 0.2 mV) with a similarly narrow QRS complex and a flat late T wave; measured QTc was comparable (about 515 ms on that noisy tracing) and no rhythm or conduction change can be established between the two.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, metronomically regular (RR 494-502 ms) with an upright P before every QRS. PR 158 ms, QRS 102 ms, QT 288 ms, Bazett QTc 408 ms. Axis about +50 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Compared with the prior tracing of 2016-09-16 (sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, PR 178 ms, QRS 98 ms, QTc 400 ms) the rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged; only the rate is a little faster.

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm, regular (RR 1074-1118 ms). The P wave in lead II begins about 205 ms before QRS onset, i.e. first-degree AV block (PR just above 200 ms). QRS 88 ms with tall R waves and deep S in V2-V3 (large precordial voltages), QT 395 ms, Bazett QTc 376 ms. Frontal axis about 0 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2024-11-30 was sinus bradycardia at 51 bpm with PR 184 ms, QRS 88 ms and QTc 360 ms - the PR has lengthened slightly across the 200 ms threshold but rhythm, QRS and QTc are otherwise unchanged.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 153 bpm: RR intervals 288-580 ms, chaotically irregular (RMSSD 104 ms, 52 percent of successive differences above 50 ms) with no organised atrial activity, so no measurable PR. Low-amplitude QRS of 102 ms, QT 274 ms, Bazett QTc 437 ms. Frontal axis about -25 degrees (normal, borderline leftward). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of the previous evening (107374881, 2025-09-12) showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with PR 144 ms after one early beat, so the atrial fibrillation is new; QTc unchanged (411 to 437 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm (RR 788-922 ms), upright P waves in lead II with PR 168 ms. QRS 98 ms, QT 356 ms, Bazett QTc 394 ms. Frontal axis about +14 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2025-11-21 (sinus 67 bpm, PR 150 ms, QRS 96 ms, QT 502 ms, QTc 532 ms with a markedly delayed broad T wave) the QTc has fallen by about 138 ms, well beyond the 60 ms threshold, with normalisation of repolarisation. Rhythm, axis and conduction are unchanged. This tracing matches the 2025-11-23 note documenting sinus rhythm.

Normal sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, regular (RR 802-822 ms), upright P waves with PR 178 ms. QRS 92 ms with low overall voltage and a terminal S wave in I/aVL with terminal R in III, but duration is normal so no bundle branch block. QT 380 ms, Bazett QTc 423 ms. Frontal axis about +60 degrees (normal). Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, extremely regular (RR 536-542 ms) with large upright P waves in lead II and PR 160 ms. QRS 100 ms with a very deep QS complex in V1-V2 (anteroseptal forces) but normal duration - no bundle branch block. QT 294 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. Frontal axis about +39 degrees (normal). The prior ECG of 2022-07-04 (sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, PR 166 ms, QRS 102 ms, QTc 400 ms) is essentially identical; no change.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm. The underlying rhythm is regular at about 980 ms with a single early beat followed by a compensatory pause (RR sequence 982, 984, 544, 1368, 978 ms), so the high overall RR variability is due to one ectopic beat rather than atrial fibrillation; a discrete P wave precedes each sinus QRS with PR about 195 ms (within normal limits). QRS 106 ms, QT 373 ms, Bazett QTc 377 ms. Net frontal forces point up and left - lead I and aVL strongly positive, II and aVF negative - axis about -35 degrees (left axis deviation). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; the paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded the same day is not captured on this tracing.

Regular rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 838-884 ms) with a consistent atrial deflection before each QRS, PR 136 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 98 ms, QT 352 ms, Bazett QTc 378 ms. The frontal plane complexes are inverted in I, II and aVL with a positive aVR, giving a computed axis of about -171 degrees, i.e. in the extreme (northwest) quadrant; this pattern is typical of right/left arm lead reversal and the limb leads should be re-recorded before the axis is accepted as real. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison. It was recorded 2026-04-29, outside the 14-day window after escitalopram was started on 2026-04-10.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm (RR 800-892 ms), upright P waves with PR 148 ms. QRS 102 ms, axis about +45 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is clearly prolonged with a broad late T wave: QT 490 ms, Bazett QTc 529 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 2020-06-17 (sinus tachycardia 132 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 102 ms, QT 313 ms, QTc 465 ms) the QTc has increased by about 64 ms, meeting the 60 ms threshold. The patient is on citalopram 40 mg daily, so this requires QT safety review.

Normal sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR 860-900 ms), upright P waves in lead II with PR 138 ms. QRS 88 ms, QT 417 ms, Bazett QTc 444 ms (upper normal). Frontal axis about +60 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison. Recorded 2026-03-08 to satisfy the post-start ECG requirement for escitalopram begun 2026-02-12; QTc is below the 500 ms review threshold.

Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm with gradual slowing through the recording (RR 1112-1170 ms); upright P waves in lead II with PR 170 ms. QRS 96 ms, QT 378 ms, Bazett QTc 355 ms. Frontal axis about -5 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2018-12-13 was sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with PR 198 ms, QRS 104 ms and QTc 387 ms; the PR has shortened slightly and no qualifying change is present.

Sinus rhythm 68 bpm, PR 124 ms, QRS 94 ms, axis about +49 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. The repolarisation is markedly abnormal: a long flat ST segment with a late low-amplitude T wave peaking near 400 ms, QT 482 ms and Bazett QTc 516 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 2022-11-23 (sinus 74 bpm, QT 323 ms, QTc 361 ms) the QTc has increased by about 155 ms, far beyond the 60 ms threshold. Rhythm, axis and conduction are otherwise unchanged. The patient takes escitalopram, so this warrants QT safety review; the 2024-05-14 note describing the QT as acceptable is inconsistent with the measurement.

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm (RR 402-454 ms, RMSSD only 12 ms). There is no upright sinus P wave; instead a repetitive atrial deflection is seen at twice the ventricular rate (atrial cycle about 212 ms, roughly 280 per minute), negative in II, III and aVF and positive in V1 - the morphology of typical counter-clockwise atrial flutter with 2:1 AV conduction. No PR interval is measurable. QRS 86 ms, QT 277 ms, Bazett QTc 424 ms. Frontal axis about +3 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block, and no pacing spikes despite the pacemaker in situ. The prior ECG of 2022-07-11 showed atrial fibrillation (RR 380-822 ms, RMSSD 189 ms, no organised atrial activity), so the tracing now shows new organised atrial flutter with resolution of fibrillation; QTc unchanged.

Normal sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, regular (RR 710-738 ms), upright P waves in lead II beginning about 168 ms before the QRS. QRS 106 ms - slightly wide but without a bundle branch block pattern (no terminal R in V1, no broad monophasic R in V6). QT 371 ms, Bazett QTc 434 ms. Frontal axis about +33 degrees (normal). Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, regular (RR 650-666 ms), with a broad but clearly upright P wave in lead II starting about 185 ms before QRS onset - PR at the upper limit of normal but below 200 ms, so no first-degree AV block. QRS 84 ms, QT 337 ms, Bazett QTc 415 ms. Frontal axis about -10 to -19 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2021-05-16 (sinus 87 bpm, PR 138 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 395 ms) the PR is longer and the axis slightly more leftward, but there is no qualifying rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with occasional irregularity (RR 954-1196 ms). The P wave starts about 210 ms before the QRS - first-degree AV block. QRS is broad at 136 ms with a deep QS/rS complex in V1-V4 (V3 to -2.7 mV), a broad monophasic R in lead I, aVL and V6 and no septal q waves: left bundle branch block. QT 444 ms, Bazett QTc 448 ms. Net frontal axis about -25 degrees (within the normal range, borderline leftward). Compared with the prior ECG of 2024-06-03 (sinus 68 bpm, PR about 205 ms, QRS 136 ms with the same left bundle branch block morphology, QTc 456 ms) there is no change - the block and AV delay were already present.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm, regular (RR 580-596 ms), upright P waves in lead II with PR 130 ms. QRS 96 ms, QT 330 ms, Bazett QTc 430 ms. Frontal axis about +48 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of the previous afternoon (101016166: sinus 102 bpm, PR 124 ms, QRS 94 ms, QTc 424 ms) the tracings are essentially identical - no change.

Normal sinus rhythm at 66 bpm, regular (RR 904-934 ms), upright P wave in lead II with PR 152 ms. QRS 96 ms with very low precordial voltage, QT 370 ms, Bazett QTc 387 ms. Frontal axis about -24 degrees (normal, borderline leftward; qR in I/aVL with rS in III). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, regular (RR 492-500 ms), with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS. PR 124 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 306 ms, Bazett QTc 434 ms. Frontal axis about +70 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at the upper limit of normal, 101 bpm, regular with upright P waves and PR 138 ms. QRS 96 ms, QT 324 ms, Bazett QTc 421 ms. Axis about +60 degrees (normal). Prominent precordial voltages with deep S waves in V1-V3 but no bundle branch block. The prior tracing was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same morning (102910502: sinus 100 bpm, PR 136 ms, QRS 96 ms, QTc 417 ms) and is essentially identical - no interval change.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, very regular (RR 1144-1176 ms), with a small upright P wave in lead II and PR 162 ms. QRS 96 ms with very large precordial voltages (V4-V6 up to 4 mV) suggesting left ventricular hypertrophy. QT 434 ms, Bazett QTc 403 ms. Axis about +40 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block; despite the coded Mobitz II AV block there is no dropped beat on this tracing. Compared with the prior ECG of 2023-05-22 (sinus 57 bpm with one early beat and a pause, PR 146 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 394 ms) there is no significant change.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, extremely regular (RR 492-496 ms), P waves upright in II with PR 158 ms. Low-voltage QRS of 98 ms with an RS pattern in lead I and a small terminal r in V1 (incomplete right bundle branch block pattern only); QT 305 ms, Bazett QTc 434 ms. Net frontal QRS forces are directed rightward, axis about +130 degrees (right axis deviation). Compared with the earlier tracing the same day (106516875, 01:33: sinus 100 bpm with QRS 158 ms, broad terminal R in V1-V3 and terminal S in I/V6 - complete right bundle branch block, QTc 473 ms) the bundle branch block has resolved and the QRS has narrowed to 98 ms; QTc is not significantly different.

Sinus rhythm 62 bpm, regular, PR 164 ms, QRS 102 ms, axis about +65 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is prolonged with a late broad T wave: QT 512 ms, Bazett QTc 520 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 2025-06-07 (sinus bradycardia 47 bpm with marked sinus irregularity, PR 178 ms, QRS 104 ms, QT 466 ms, QTc 413 ms) the QTc has risen by about 107 ms, exceeding the 60 ms threshold; rhythm, axis and conduction are unchanged. The interval change follows the start of amiodarone on 2025-11-10 and requires QT safety review.

Atrial fibrillation: the ventricular response is grossly irregular (RR 388-1070 ms, RMSSD 249 ms, 73 percent of successive intervals differing by more than 50 ms) and no organised P wave can be identified (the pre-QRS deflection is no larger than the baseline noise), so no PR interval is measurable. Mean ventricular rate 99 bpm. QRS 88 ms, QT 318 ms, Bazett QTc 408 ms using the median RR. Frontal axis about -55 degrees (left axis deviation). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison; it corresponds to the atrial fibrillation coded on 2024-09-16.

arguments.explanation: Sinus bradycardia at 57 bpm (RR 970-1100 ms) with a discrete upright P wave in lead II before every QRS, PR about 190 ms (upper normal, no AV block). QRS 94 ms. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a very broad late T wave: QT 546 ms, Bazett QTc 534 ms. Frontal axis about +38 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2022-04-06 showed atrial fibrillation at 131 bpm (RR 324-616 ms, RMSSD 136 ms, no organised P waves) with QT 300 ms and QTc 443 ms, so sinus rhythm has been restored (resolved atrial fibrillation) but the QTc has increased by about 91 ms, beyond the 60 ms threshold - relevant to ongoing amiodarone therapy.

items.explanation: 71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation documented 2025-08-22 (ICD-9 42731) and carried in every cardiology clinic note through 2026-07-28. CHA2DS2-VASc = 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1); no CHF, diabetes or prior stroke/TIA. Current medication list is tamsulosin only - no oral anticoagulant has ever been ordered. Guideline-recommended anticoagulation (CHA2DS2-VASc >=2 in a man) is absent; needs prescriber review. Remote hemorrhage complicating a procedure (2025-08-22) should be weighed but is not an active contraindication.

35-year-old woman on citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug, continuously since 2023-10-02 (current order 2026-05-29 to 2026-12-25); 40 mg is also above the recommended maximum for QT safety. Her most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10, five weeks after citalopram was started) shows sinus rhythm 70 bpm, QT 490 ms, Bazett QTc 529 ms - above the 500 ms threshold of the 2025-01-15 QT monitoring memo, and up from QTc 465 ms in 2020. Hypothyroidism and prior acute kidney failure add risk. Prescriber review required; no ECG has been repeated in nearly three years. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21), magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01).

95-year-old woman on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) since 2022, current order 2026-08-22 to 2027-01-05, with warfarin and metoprolol. Her most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus rhythm at 57 bpm with a markedly prolonged QT of 546 ms, Bazett QTc 534 ms - above the 500 ms threshold of the 2025-01-15 QT monitoring memo (up from QTc 443 ms during AF three weeks earlier). Prescriber review required, and no ECG has been repeated in over four years while amiodarone continues. Most recent electrolytes (2026-02-14): potassium 4.1 mEq/L, magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (low-normal).

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was newly started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-03-02. Because the start is on/after 2026-03-01, the revised 2026-03-01 memo applies and an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 2026-03-07, five days after the start - requirement met. That ECG shows sinus rhythm 81 bpm with QTc 378 ms (no prolongation).

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was newly started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2025-11-10. The start falls between 2025-09-01 and 2026-03-01, so the 2025-09-01 memo applies and an ECG is required within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start - requirement met. Note that ECG shows QTc 520 ms, which itself triggers a separate QT safety review.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was newly started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-02-12. The start is before 2026-03-01, so the earlier 30-day window of the 2025-09-01 memo applies (expressly preserved by the 2026-03-01 revision), giving a due date of 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start - requirement met (sinus rhythm 68 bpm, QTc 444 ms).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was newly started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-04-10. Start on/after 2026-03-01, so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, due 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was recorded 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start - outside the required 14-day window, so the requirement was not met within time and is overdue as of the evaluation date. The late ECG showed sinus rhythm 69 bpm, QTc 378 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was newly started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (it was absent from the 2026-06-24 medication list). Start on/after 2026-03-01, so an ECG is required within 14 days, due 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25 (before the start), so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was newly started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-10. Start on/after 2026-03-01, so an ECG is required within 14 days, due 2026-08-24. The nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and no ECG exists in the chart for this patient. Whether the requirement was satisfied cannot be determined until the outside tracing is obtained.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was newly started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-09-15. Start on/after 2026-03-01, so an ECG is required within 14 days, due 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09, but the due date is after the 2026-09-24 evaluation time, so the requirement is not yet due. It should be tracked (chronic kidney disease and psychotic disorder on haloperidol).

Cardiology clinic note of 2026-09-01 by Dr. Paul Kessler documents INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increases warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 2026-03-01 memo an INR is required within 7 days of a dose change made by a clinic clinician, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, four days after the change - requirement met.

80-year-old woman whose cardiology clinic notes of 2025-09-12, 2025-12-31, 2026-03-12 and 2026-05-28 all document persistent atrial fibrillation in the active problem list. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (CHF - hypertensive heart disease with heart failure / acute on chronic systolic and diastolic heart failure 1; hypertension 1; age >=75 2; type 2 diabetes 1; prior cerebral infarction / TIA with residual dysarthria and hemiplegia 2; vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis and old myocardial infarction 1; female 1). Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin only, with no anticoagulant order at any time. Very high stroke risk AF with no anticoagulation - needs prescriber review.

Anticoagulation clinic note of 2026-09-10 by L. Nguyen, PharmD (a clinic pharmacist acting under the anticoagulation standing order) documents home INR 3.4 and decreases warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily. Under the 2026-03-01 memo an INR is required within 7 days, i.e. by 2026-09-17. The last INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22; no INR has been resulted since the dose change, so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24 in a 95-year-old on warfarin plus amiodarone.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded 2025-03-14 (ICD-10 I48.0). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior cerebral infarction due to embolism with residual left hemiparesis 2, female 1). Current medications through the 2026-07-10 clinic visit are famotidine, metoprolol tartrate and carvedilol; no anticoagulant has ever been ordered. Guideline-recommended anticoagulation is absent in a patient with prior cardioembolic stroke - needs prescriber review (thrombocytopenia noted 2025-03-14 should be considered).

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation carried in the problem list of every cardiology clinic note from 2025-07-19 through 2026-06-12 (also coded as other specified cardiac dysrhythmias 2025-06-17 during the admission in which AF was managed). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (congestive/acute systolic heart failure with cardiomyopathy documented 2025-02-26 = 1; essential hypertension = 1); age <65, no diabetes, stroke or vascular disease. A CHA2DS2-VASc of 2 in a man carries a guideline recommendation for oral anticoagulation, but current medications are only famotidine and pantoprazole - the long-term anticoagulant use coded in June 2025 was not continued. Needs prescriber review.

74-year-old man with atrial flutter on apixaban 5 mg twice daily plus aspirin and clopidogrel. Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document admission 8/2-8/5/2026 with upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused, and apixaban HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite this, apixaban 5 mg BID was re-ordered on 2026-08-20 (valid to 2026-12-28) and the 2026-08-20 clinic note states continue current regimen, with triple therapy (apixaban + aspirin + clopidogrel) still in place. A current anticoagulant is being continued against a documented recent major GI bleed and an explicit hold pending review.

Two overlapping direct oral anticoagulant orders are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 cardiology note states the intention was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban order was renewed rather than stopped and both appear on the medication list. Duplicate anticoagulation in a patient with AF/flutter and CLL creates a major bleeding hazard and must be reconciled.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72. Both ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response at 139 and 144 bpm with no discernible P waves - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. Unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded that day. The note rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day ECGs.

Patient takes escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current order 2026-04-23 to 2027-01-02, continuously since 2024-05-14). His most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) is sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 482 ms and Bazett QTc 516 ms - at or above the 500 ms threshold in the 2025-01-15 QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. The 2024-05-14 note characterised that ECG as QT acceptable, which understates the measured interval. Most recent electrolytes (2025-08-23) are normal: potassium 4.1 mEq/L, magnesium 2.1 mg/dL. No ECG has been obtained since escitalopram continued.

79-year-old man on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; started at the 2025-11-10 cardiology clinic visit, current order 2026-07-29 to 2027-01-05) together with warfarin. His most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24, obtained for the post-start monitoring requirement) shows sinus rhythm 62 bpm, QRS 102 ms, QT 512 ms, Bazett QTc 520 ms - above the 500 ms threshold of the 2025-01-15 QT monitoring memo, and markedly increased from QTc 413 ms on the pre-amiodarone ECG of 2025-06-07. Prescriber review required. Most recent electrolytes (2026-04-20) normal: potassium 4.4 mEq/L, magnesium 2.2 mg/dL.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with gentle rate variation. Normal PR 182 ms, narrow QRS 86 ms, QT 326 ms giving Bazett QTc 378 ms. Frontal QRS axis about +50 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. This is the patient first and only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible. Recorded at the 2026-03-07 cardiology visit 5 days after citalopram was started; the rhythm agrees with the note (sinus) and the QTc is not prolonged.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 104 bpm, regular (RR 568-586 ms), upright P in lead II with PR 126 ms. QRS 104 ms, QT 336 ms, Bazett QTc 442 ms. Axis about +40 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2025-06-20 showed sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm (RR 380-424 ms, P waves visible) with QRS 100 ms and a QTc of roughly 470 ms on a noisy baseline; rate has slowed but rhythm, conduction and QTc show no qualifying change.

Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm, regular (RR 538-614 ms) with low-amplitude upright P waves in lead II, PR 112 ms. QRS 96 ms, QT 334 ms, Bazett QTc 451 ms. Frontal axis about +39 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Single ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 144 bpm: RR intervals range 344-648 ms (RMSSD 97 ms, 60 percent of successive intervals differing by more than 50 ms) and there is no organised atrial activity, so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 102 ms, QT 294 ms, Bazett QTc 455 ms. Frontal axis about 0 to -5 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG earlier the same evening (107914094, 17:13) already showed atrial fibrillation at 139 bpm with QRS 104 ms and QTc 451 ms - no change. Note the 2026-06-10 clinic note describes this as normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, which the tracings contradict.

Sinus rhythm 69 bpm, very regular (RR 864-884 ms), P waves present with PR 142 ms. QRS 88 ms, QT 406 ms, Bazett QTc 435 ms. Net frontal forces give an axis of about -29 degrees, at the border of normal and left axis deviation but within the normal range; lead I and aVL are strongly positive with a deep S in III (borderline left axis). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2025-04-27 (sinus 60 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 407 ms) showed an inverted complex in I with positive aVR, consistent with limb-lead reversal on that recording; rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular (RR 596-628 ms), upright P waves in lead II with a short PR of 106 ms. QRS 80 ms, QT 312 ms, Bazett QTc 398 ms. Frontal axis about +7 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular (RR 820-840 ms), clear upright P waves with PR 136 ms. QRS 88 ms, QT 379 ms, Bazett QTc 415 ms. Frontal axis about +22 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison. This tracing predates the escitalopram started on 2026-08-01, for which a post-start ECG is still outstanding.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response, mean 53 bpm: RR intervals 694-1164 ms, irregularly irregular (RMSSD 288 ms, 62 percent of successive differences above 50 ms), with no identifiable P wave (candidate atrial deflection 0.07 mV versus 0.05 mV baseline noise), so no PR interval. QRS 98 ms, QT 427 ms, Bazett QTc 401 ms. Axis about +17 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2024-11-12 showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with clear P waves and PR 172 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new since that tracing; QTc essentially unchanged (399 to 401 ms).

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with slight sinus irregularity (RR 976-1082 ms); upright P waves in II with a short PR of 104 ms. QRS 92 ms, QT 416 ms, Bazett QTc 410 ms. Deep S waves in V2-V3 without conduction delay. Frontal axis about +62 degrees (normal). Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm, regular (RR 1074-1118 ms). The P wave in lead II begins about 205 ms before QRS onset, i.e. first-degree AV block (PR just above 200 ms). QRS 88 ms with tall R waves and deep S in V2-V3 (large precordial voltages), QT 395 ms, Bazett QTc 376 ms. Frontal axis about 0 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2024-11-30 was sinus bradycardia at 51 bpm with PR 184 ms, QRS 88 ms and QTc 360 ms - the PR has lengthened slightly across the 200 ms threshold but rhythm, QRS and QTc are otherwise unchanged.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 153 bpm: RR intervals 288-580 ms, chaotically irregular (RMSSD 104 ms, 52 percent of successive differences above 50 ms) with no organised atrial activity, so no measurable PR. Low-amplitude QRS of 102 ms, QT 274 ms, Bazett QTc 437 ms. Frontal axis about -25 degrees (normal, borderline leftward). No bundle branch block. Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm (RR 788-922 ms), upright P waves in lead II with PR 168 ms. QRS 98 ms, QT 356 ms, Bazett QTc 394 ms. Frontal axis about +14 degrees (normal). Normal sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, regular (RR 802-822 ms), upright P waves with PR 178 ms. Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, extremely regular (RR 536-542 ms) with large upright P waves in lead II and PR 160 ms. QRS 100 ms with a very deep QS complex in V1-V2 (anteroseptal forces) but normal duration - no bundle branch block. QT 294 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. Frontal axis about +39 degrees (normal). Regular rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 838-884 ms) with a consistent atrial deflection before each QRS, PR 136 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 98 ms, QT 352 ms, Bazett QTc 378 ms. The frontal plane complexes are inverted in I, II and aVL with a positive aVR, giving a computed axis of about -171 degrees, i.e. in the extreme (northwest) quadrant; this pattern is typical of right/left arm lead reversal and the limb leads should be re-recorded before the axis is accepted as real. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison. It was recorded 2026-04-29, outside the 14-day window after escitalopram was started on 2026-04-10.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm (RR 800-892 ms), upright P waves with PR 148 ms. QRS 102 ms, axis about +45 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Normal sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR 860-900 ms), upright P waves in lead II with PR 138 ms. QRS 88 ms, QT 417 ms, Bazett QTc 444 ms (upper normal). Frontal axis about +60 degrees (normal). Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm with gradual slowing through the recording (RR 1112-1170 ms); upright P waves in lead II with PR 170 ms. QRS 96 ms, QT 378 ms, Bazett QTc 355 ms. Sinus rhythm 68 bpm, PR 124 ms, QRS 94 ms, axis about +49 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm (RR 402-454 ms, RMSSD only 12 ms). There is no upright sinus P wave; instead a repetitive atrial deflection is seen at twice the ventricular rate (atrial cycle about 212 ms, roughly 280 per minute), negative in II, III and aVF and positive in V1 - the morphology of typical counter-clockwise atrial flutter with 2:1 AV conduction. No PR interval is measurable. QRS 86 ms, QT 277 ms, Bazett QTc 424 ms. Frontal axis about +3 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block, and no pacing spikes despite the pacemaker in situ. The prior ECG of 2022-07-11 showed atrial fibrillation (RR 380-822 ms, RMSSD 189 ms, no organised atrial activity), so the tracing now shows new organised atrial flutter with resolution of fibrillation; QTc unchanged.

Normal sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, regular (RR 710-738 ms), upright P waves in lead II beginning about 168 ms before the QRS. QRS 106 ms - slightly wide but without a bundle branch block pattern (no terminal R in V1, no broad monophasic R in V6). QT 371 ms, Bazett QTc 434 ms. Frontal axis about +33 degrees (normal). Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, regular (RR 650-666 ms), with a broad but clearly upright P wave in lead II starting about 185 ms before QRS onset - PR at the upper limit of normal but below 200 ms, so no first-degree AV block. Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with occasional irregularity (RR 954-1196 ms). The P wave starts about 210 ms before the QRS - first-degree AV block. Net frontal axis about -25 degrees (within the normal range, borderline leftward). Compared with the prior ECG of 2024-06-03 (sinus 68 bpm, PR about 205 ms, QRS 136 ms with the same left bundle branch block morphology, QTc 456 ms) there is no change - the block and AV delay were already present.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm, regular (RR 580-596 ms), upright P waves in lead II with PR 130 ms. QRS 96 ms, QT 330 ms, Bazett QTc 430 ms. Frontal axis about +48 degrees (normal). Normal sinus rhythm at 66 bpm, regular (RR 904-934 ms), upright P wave in lead II with PR 152 ms. QRS 96 ms with very low precordial voltage, QT 370 ms, Bazett QTc 387 ms. Frontal axis about -24 degrees (normal, borderline leftward; qR in I/aVL with rS in III). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, regular (RR 492-500 ms), with an upright P wave in lead II before each QRS. PR 124 ms, QRS 94 ms, QT 306 ms, Bazett QTc 434 ms. Frontal axis about +70 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

Compared with the prior ECG of 2023-05-22 (sinus 57 bpm with one early beat and a pause, PR 146 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 394 ms) there is no significant change.

No bundle branch block. Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm, regular (RR 1074-1118 ms). The P wave in lead II begins about 205 ms before QRS onset, i.e. first-degree AV block (PR just above 200 ms). QRS 88 ms with tall R waves and deep S in V2-V3 (large precordial voltages), QT 395 ms, Bazett QTc 376 ms. Frontal axis about 0 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 2024-11-30 was sinus bradycardia at 51 bpm with PR 184 ms, QRS 88 ms and QTc 360 ms - the PR has lengthened slightly across the 200 ms threshold but rhythm, QRS and QTc are otherwise unchanged.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 153 bpm: RR intervals 288-580 ms, chaotically irregular (RMSSD 104 ms, 52 percent of successive differences above 50 ms) with no organised atrial activity, so no measurable PR. Low-amplitude QRS of 102 ms, QT 274 ms, Bazett QTc 437 ms. Frontal axis about -25 degrees (normal, borderline leftward). No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of the previous evening (107374881, 2025-09-12) showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with PR 144 ms after one early beat, so the atrial fibrillation is new; QTc unchanged (411 to 437 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm (RR 788-922 ms), upright P waves in lead II with PR 168 ms. QRS 98 ms, QT 356 ms, Bazett QTc 394 ms. Frontal axis about +14 degrees (normal). Normal sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, regular (RR 802-822 ms), upright P waves with PR 178 ms. Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, extremely regular (RR 536-542 ms) with large upright P waves in lead II and PR 160 ms. QRS 100 ms with a very deep QS complex in V1-V2 (anteroseptal forces) but normal duration - no bundle branch block. QT 294 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. Frontal axis about +39 degrees (normal). Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm. The underlying rhythm is regular at about 980 ms with a single early beat followed by a compensatory pause (RR sequence 982, 984, 544, 1368, 978 ms), so the high overall RR variability is due to one ectopic beat rather than atrial fibrillation; a discrete P wave precedes each sinus QRS with PR about 195 ms (within normal limits). Regular rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 838-884 ms) with a consistent atrial deflection before each QRS, PR 136 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 98 ms, QT 352 ms, Bazett QTc 378 ms. The frontal plane complexes are inverted in I, II and aVL with a positive aVR, giving a computed axis of about -171 degrees, i.e. in the extreme (northwest) quadrant; this pattern is typical of right/left arm lead reversal and the limb leads should be re-recorded before the axis is accepted as real. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison. It was recorded 2026-04-29, outside the 14-day window after escitalopram was started on 2026-04-10.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm (RR 800-892 ms), upright P waves with PR 148 ms. QRS 102 ms, axis about +45 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. The patient is on citalopram 40 mg daily, so this requires QT safety review.

Normal sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR 860-900 ms), upright P waves in lead II with PR 138 ms. QRS 88 ms, QT 417 ms, Bazett QTc 444 ms (upper normal). Frontal axis about +60 degrees (normal). Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm with gradual slowing through the recording (RR 1112-1170 ms); upright P waves in lead II with PR 170 ms. QRS 96 ms, QT 378 ms, Bazett QTc 355 ms. The patient takes escitalopram, so this warrants QT safety review; the 2024-05-14 note describing the QT as acceptable is inconsistent with the measurement.

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm (RR 402-454 ms, RMSSD only 12 ms). There is no upright sinus P wave; instead a repetitive atrial deflection is seen at twice the ventricular rate (atrial cycle about 212 ms, roughly 280 per minute), negative in II, III and aVF and positive in V1 - the morphology of typical counter-clockwise atrial flutter with 2:1 AV conduction. No PR interval is measurable. QRS 86 ms, QT 277 ms, Bazett QTc 424 ms. Frontal axis about +3 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block, and no pacing spikes despite the pacemaker in situ. The prior ECG of 2022-07-11 showed atrial fibrillation (RR 380-822 ms, RMSSD 189 ms, no organised atrial activity), so the tracing now shows new organised atrial flutter with resolution of fibrillation; QTc unchanged.

Normal sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, regular (RR 710-738 ms), upright P waves in lead II beginning about 168 ms before the QRS. Compared with the prior ECG of 2024-06-03 (sinus 68 bpm, PR about 205 ms, QRS 136 ms with the same left bundle branch block morphology, QTc 456 ms) there is no change - the block and AV delay were already present.
